transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I'm here because my sleep has basically just fallen apart. I'll get into bed at my apartment, close my laptop, and... I just lie there for hours. My brain just keeps mentally rechecking work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments. I just can't shut it down. And then, even when I actually do manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling like my mind never really turned off. I'm just exhausted.
Outside of when you are trying to fall asleep, do you find that you spend a significant amount of your day worrying about these various responsibilities and tasks?

Yeah, it's... pretty much all day, honestly. My mind just keeps jumping from one thing to another. Like, I'll worry about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then it immediately shifts to whether I'm wasting money on school. Or I'll start thinking about whether my family will think I just can't handle things. It's like I treat every single small issue that comes up like it could completely derail my whole future.
Have you noticed that you've lost interest or pleasure in doing the things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I still enjoy the things I normally like to do. Um, I might not do them as often right now just because I'm so exhausted from not sleeping, or because my mind is distracted by everything else... but the actual interest is definitely still there.
Do you often feel physically tense, such as having tight muscles, a clenched jaw, or a feeling of being 'on edge' throughout the day?

Um, no, I haven't really noticed my muscles feeling tight or anything like that. I don't think I clench my jaw, either. Honestly, my body mostly just feels heavy and tired from not sleeping well. Any feeling of being on edge is really just... in my head, with my thoughts racing, rather than physical tension.
How long have you been experiencing these persistent, racing worries about your daily life?

It's been about a year and three months now. It started right around the time I began my evening graduate certificate program while still working my full-time analyst job. That's when all this really kicked in.
When these thoughts and worries start to consume your mind, do you find that you are able to stop or push them aside, or do they feel uncontrollable?

They definitely feel uncontrollable. I mean, I try to tell myself to just stop and focus on one thing, but... it doesn't really work. One worry just immediately leads to another. Before I know it, I'm checking my calendar, and then my budget, and then my school assignments over and over again, instead of actually getting anything done.
Do you often feel restless, or as if you are keyed up or on edge, even if you don't feel physical tension in your muscles?

I wouldn't say I feel restless or keyed up, no. Like I mentioned, it's really just the racing thoughts. My body doesn't feel on edge, it just feels exhausted. I don't feel like I need to pace or move around or anything like that.
When you are dealing with these persistent worries, do you find that your mind frequently goes blank or that you have difficulty concentrating on the tasks you are trying to complete?

Yes, definitely. I have a lot of trouble concentrating. I’ll stare at the same financial model for work, or a reading for my classes, for ages. Then I'll realize I’ve reread the same paragraph like five times without actually absorbing any of it, just because my head is already off running through everything that could go wrong.
Do you find that you have been more irritable or quick-tempered than usual since these worries started?
No, I haven't really noticed being more irritable. I don't think I've been snapping at anyone or losing my temper more than usual. It's mostly just the worrying and the exhaustion.
Has this constant worrying and difficulty concentrating caused you to have any problems with your job performance or your relationships with others?

Yes, it definitely has. I've actually started missing work deadlines, which isn't like me at all. And I'm falling behind in my certificate classes, too. It's just hard to keep up when I can't focus. I've also completely stopped doing the things that used to help keep me grounded... like, I haven't been doing yoga or running, and I used to cook a lot, but I just don't have the energy for any of that anymore.
